lines.ruling: Ruling: model error; f1040s1a (2025), line 36a: "If you have a valid social security number (see instructions) and were born before January 2, 1961, enter the amount from line 35", with the spouse on line 36b; i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d, separates the boxes for you and for your spouse. sa.age65 is the published question "Were you born before January 2, 1961?" for you alone (its consumer is Schedule 1-A line 36a); the candidate reads it as whether any line 12d box (age or blindness, yours or a joint spouse's) is checked. The 17 completed-return value differences (project false, candidate true) are returns where you were not born before January 2, 1961 but your joint spouse was, or (classm.tcw.16) your spouse is blind: classm.f8962.5.deepseek (spouse age 65 or older, you not), classm.f8962.5.gpt, classm.scveh.1, classm.tcw.16, mutation.t2.f8962_months_asset3, generated returns 208, 254, 255, 290, 366, 373, 395 and 476, and four partial records of classm.f8962.5.gpt (sa.spouse_extra, sa.spouse_itemizes, sa.elect_itemize or sa.gambling_losses withheld). Triage executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/sa.json`; 1,495 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 526 partial records from 40 bases; 2,521 comparisons): 2,427 agree; differences 17 candidate-unknown, 77 value; on completed returns 17 value; every completed-return witness enumerated by an uncapped scratch rerun of the same evaluator (the record keeps 6 per kind). Project stands.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d: "If your filing status is married filing separately and your spouse was born before January 2, 1961, or was blind at the end of 2025, you can check the appropriate box(es) on line 12d if your spouse had no income, isn’t filing a return, and can’t be claimed as a dependent on another person’s return"; p. 34, Line 12e: "In most cases, your federal income tax will be less if you take the larger of your standard deduction or itemized deductions"; Schedule A (2025), line 18: "If you elect to itemize deductions even though they are less than your standard deduction, check this box". executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/sa.json`, pass 3adda1bd8137; 1,702 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 509 partial records; 2,711 comparisons): 2,464 of 2,711 agree; differences 222 candidate-unknown, 24 candidate-refuses, 1 value; on returns the full interview completes: 148 candidate-unknown, 6 candidate-refuses; witnesses enumerated with the cap lifted (scratch /tmp/adj/tr/eicwork/full/sa.json). The completed candidate-unknowns on sa.spouse_extra (144 on sa.itemizes, 148 on sa.deduction) are all on returns that are not married filing separately (on sa.deduction's 148: single 65, head of household 29, joint 28, qualifying surviving spouse 9 among the fixtures, 17 partial records): the candidate reads sa.spouse_extra through its standard deduction (sa.h_standard) for every status, while the source's spouse-box rule is for a separate return only and the project asks it only then (sa.mfs_spouse_extra); married filing separately is itself refused (s3.mfs at scope.ready). The 6 completed candidate-refusals are classm.clcw.2, classm.clcw.2.deepseek, mutation.t2.no_senior_part5 and three partials of classm.clcw.2.deepseek: single returns whose record answers sa.spouse_extra Yes to a question that opens "Married filing separately", which the interview does not ask a single filer; the project itemizes there ($52,023.83 against a $15,750.00 standard deduction). A candidate that needs an answer, or refuses on one, that the source does not need is a model error (README). The other 4 completed candidate-unknowns need sa.elect_itemize on partial records (classm.s3.1.deepseek, classm.f8962.4.deepseek, classm.s8812.1.deepseek, classm.f5695.1.deepseek with the election withheld) whose line 17 exceeds the standard deduction, where the source itemizes without the election (project true). The 1 value difference is stage4.standard.spouse_itemizes, a refused married-filing-separately record with line 17 and the standard deduction both $0 (the deduction is $0 either way): scope. The rest are on incomplete or refused records. Gate-wave check: sa.mfs_spouse_extra, sa.mfs_spouse_itemizes and sa.boxes_age65 (all, now choose or person.age65_box) give the same sa.itemizes, sa.deduction and Form 1040 line 12e in HEAD and the working tree on every completed return (1,702 fixtures and 500 generated returns evaluated in both trees; classm.clcw.2 evaluated in both). As the earlier ruling on this line. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; i1040sca p. 11, Line 16, "Gambling losses (gambling losses include, but aren't limited to, the cost of nonwinning bingo, lottery, and raffle tickets) but only to the extent of gambling winnings reported on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8b." Where both give a value the reply's amount is the project's (the smaller of the losses and line 8b); but the reply reads sa.gambling_losses on every return, where the project gives zero without winnings and the interview asks the losses only when there are winnings. So on returns with no gambling winnings the reply needs an answer the interview does not ask (candidate-unknown; the recorded witnesses name sa.gambling_losses with the project's value zero). Triage executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/sa.json`, pass 446f7398433f; 1,767 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026): 2,181 of 2,734 in-scope comparisons agree; differences by kind {"candidate-unknown": 485, "project-refuses": 63, "project-unknown": 68}; on completed returns only candidate-unknown (162); the project refusals and unknowns are on refused or incomplete records (its cited screens, and partial records withholding an answer). No value differs. The project line is retained.
